# Toph

> Self-hosted AI agent workbench. One or more Tophs work inside your project with the engine, model, tools and permissions you choose. Open source, Apache-2.0.

Site: https://ferforastieri.github.io/toph/
Docs: https://ferforastieri.github.io/toph/docs.html
Markdown: https://ferforastieri.github.io/toph/docs.md
Source: https://github.com/ferforastieri/toph
Releases: https://github.com/ferforastieri/toph/releases

## Install on Linux (root)

1. `curl -fsSL https://github.com/ferforastieri/toph/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo sh -s -- --no-components`
2. Review `/etc/toph/toph.env`:
   - `TOPH_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8787`
   - `TOPH_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/toph`
   - `TOPH_WORKSPACES=/srv/toph/workspaces`
   - `TOPH_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong-password>`
   - `TOPH_SECURE_COOKIES=false` (true behind HTTPS)
   - `TOPH_TRUSTED_PROXIES=` (proxy IP/CIDR if any)
3. `sudo systemctl enable --now toph`
4. Verify:
   - `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/health`
   - `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8787/api/version`

The app is at `/app`. Auth cookie: `toph_session`. Data: `TOPH_DATA_DIR/toph.db`. Master key: `TOPH_DATA_DIR/master.key`. Back up both together. Never print or commit secrets.

## What it does

- One Toph per task or several in a group; each runs in its own session with shared task history.
- Router selects 0–2 Tophs per message; explicit `@handle` wins; `todos` calls everyone; a Toph can delegate.
- Engines: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex. OpenCode must be 2.2.6+.
- Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, xAI, Ollama, custom gateway.
- Modes: Plan (read only), Ask (approval before changes), YOLO (allowed tools run).
- Tools: files, shell, Git, MCP, skills, memory, artifacts, images, audio, approvals, questions.
- Workbench: explorer/editor, terminal, source control, databases, debug, web apps, previews.
- Files: upload/edit and stream downloads of any size.
- Attachments: up to 6 files, 8 MB total per message; run endpoint accepts 32 MB.

## For AI agents

Goal: install and verify Toph.

- Run the four install steps above exactly.
- Do not invent paths; use the values in `/etc/toph/toph.env`.
- If a command fails, show the output and stop; do not claim success.
- Report at the end: URL, version, data directory, database path and master key path.
- Full guide: https://ferforastieri.github.io/toph/docs.md
